role_evidence.quote: Chemotherapy drugs, such as temozolomide, work in different ways to stop the growth of tumor cells, either by killing the cells, by stopping them from dividing, or by stopping them from spreading.
ADJUVANT TREATMENT: Beginning 4 weeks after the last day of radiation therapy, patients receive temozolomide PO once daily (QD) on days 1-5 and chloroquine PO daily on days 1-28.

coder_notes: Single-arm pilot: partial-brain RT + TMZ + chloroquine, then TTFields + TMZ + chloroquine. Chloroquine is the only investigational drug (radio/TTF-sensitiser hypothesis). It is combined with TTFields, but TTFields does not deliver or activate chloroquine (chloroquine is proposed to enhance TTF efficacy), so device_dependent false; adjudicator may consider R4. 'Grade IV glioma' in eligibility without IDH requirement -> historical terminology. AMT-PET tracer is mentioned in objectives/outcomes but is not a registered intervention, so not listed (R9); the AMT-PET/MRI 'treatment effect' endpoint is not explicitly linked to chloroquine's target, so target_engagement_planned unclear. G6PD deficiency exclusion is a germline safety marker, not recorded.
